source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity, but nothing in the data shows whether that power serves AI training or regulated enterprise workloads.

The 33 MW is spread across two facilities, SAT5 and SAT6, in 175,000 square feet of technical space. Its certifications are HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type 2, TIA-942, and HITRUST. Those qualify it for healthcare, federal, and payment workloads, which are baseline requirements for regulated enterprise customers rather than markers of AI specialization. Any accelerator count inferred from the 33 MW depends on an assumed rack density that the operator does not publish, so the number of racks and chips at this site is unknown.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, and only nineteen publish capacity figures. This campus ranks sixth among those nineteen and accounts for 6.9% of the state's disclosed 475 MW. That rank measures how much operators choose to disclose, not how much capacity the state actually holds. The suitability score of 68 is built from published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as the missing input.

The data does not cover grid interconnection, power source, or whether the 33 MW is allocated, under contract, or available. It does not cover GPU deployment or how power splits between training and inference. Without those facts, a 33 MW campus cannot be called a binding constraint on AI scaling, and it cannot be ruled out either. What the record establishes is a mid-sized regulated-enterprise campus in a state where most capacity goes unpublished.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
